review_method: Chronological art and frozen lettering with production captions hidden; informed implementation reviewer, other agents full-read verdicts not consulted.

inspection_timing.limitation: Includes tool round trips and prior familiarity; not naive-reader speed.

overall: A complete atmospheric missing-person pilot. The repeated phrase, failed personal-memory test, defeated mimic and nursery clue form a readable investigation. Combat/door mechanics are weaker than the mystery logic.
causal_read: Ilyra follows a personally recognizable voice into the conservatory.
A flower-shaped mimic repeats the same phrase; Neris warns that it copied her husband too.
The personal-memory question gets the same canned reply, so Ilyra rejects it as the person being sought.
A short sword exchange breaks the creature support; it falls and Neris joins Ilyra.
A recovered packet/object links the mimic to a nursery and to the missing man; they leave together to follow the lead.
strengths: Opening conservatory scale and restricted red/charcoal palette give a distinct mood from NG.
Repetition is functional evidence rather than random exposition.
The personal question reveals hurt without requiring backstory notes.
The ending identifies a concrete next destination and leaves room for the missing-person mystery.

limits.finding: Neris appears confined behind a door, but the thorn foot does not clearly pin the threshold. The exact physical reason defeating the creature frees her is inferred rather than demonstrated.
The fight reads as duck, slash and topple. A distinct defensive-guard power and exact blade/leg contact are not reliably legible at phone size.
The retrieved printed packet/drawing changes visual emphasis into a round coat-related token in the closeup; dialogue carries the connection more clearly than object continuity.
Speaker labels repair mismatched cast positions, but some dialogue remains visibly typeset around source constraints rather than naturally aimed balloons.

pacing: Short, coherent investigation beat with one brief action exchange. The delayed reveal and repeated voice support tension, though it is not a sustained horror or combat chapter.
